newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Saudi Arabia urge restraint on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: France, Saudi Arabia urge restraint on Iraq.

text.p: The foreign ministers of France and Saudi Arabia urged restraint regarding Baghdad on Tuesday, saying the people of Iraq should not be made to pay for the actions of their leaders.

"Whatever the errors of the Iraqi authorities and their incorrect analysis of the situation, the Iraqi people must not be made to suffer for this," Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal said after over an hour and a half of talks with his French counterpart Herve de Charette.
"We both agreed on the need to do all we can to lower tensions" in the region, de Charette told reporters.

Neither man referred by name to the United States, which has been threatening military action against Baghdad, accusing it of using its air defences to threaten Western surveillance flights in no-fly zones over northern and southern Iraq.
Saudi Arabia and France were part of the U.S.-led coalition that drove Iraq out of Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War, but both have distanced themselves from Washington in the latest crisis.
On another hot topic, both de Charette and Saud said they were concerned by the lack of progress in Middle East peace talks and urged a new start in the peace process.
"We hope Israel will implement the agreements already reached (and) put an end to the stagnation," Saud said.

The Saudi official said their talks were intended primarily to flesh out a bilateral agreement on economic, political and cultural cooperation reached when French President Jacques Chirac paid a two-day visit to the oil-rich desert kingdom in July.
Chirac said at the time that close ties between France and Saudi Arabia were key to the relationship Paris seeks to develop with the Arab world and nations of the Middle East in general.
France, which buys one-quarter of its oil from the kingdom, is Riyadh's third biggest arms supplier after the United States and Britain.
